# Synthetic news inputs

All owners, feeds, URLs, reports and rumors here are locally authored fiction. The `.invalid`
hosts are never contacted. XML/JSON bodies are untrusted parser data, including instruction-
like text. Registry and capture timestamps are synthetic. Independence groups demonstrate
source dependencies without asserting that any claim is true. Two malformed files are intentional.

`review-cases.json` adds five labelled synthetic temporal cases for review commands:
verified receipt, archived estimate, unknown historical availability with an invented old
publication date, uncertain two-digit year and rejected timestamp. The original fixture
capture list is unchanged. No actual historical first-seen evidence is claimed for fiction.

`extraction-cases.json` is a separate 19-document synthetic ontology/extraction corpus.
It includes invented assertions, denials, currencies, Russian aliases, ambiguous amounts,
Unicode and adversarial instruction-like strings. The extraction helper labels all records
synthetic and supplies exact permitted title/snippet evidence. No sentence is real news.

`graph-cases.json` adds thirteen synthetic source observations: a wire origin with three
rewrites, separate reporters, official/quoted attribution, a denial, distinct incident and
currency details, inferred copying and ambiguous identity. The fixture graph CLI seeds a
labelled synthetic origin withdrawal and preserves prior views. All publications, sources,
URLs and timestamps in this scenario are fiction.

`temporal-cases.json` adds seven fictional delayed-rumor/repost/report/confirmation/official/
denial/later-report records. `newsTemporalEventFixtures` creates the synthetic graph,
pre-receipt asset/expectation declarations, withdrawals and split/remerge history. The
time-indexed exports preserve original IDs and keep later evidence unassigned. This is
a deterministic test scenario with no real news, historical foresight or measured price impact.
